points.title: The comparative + S + V…, the comparative + S + V… 越...，越...
examples: The higher the cost of living is, the less willing people are to raise children.
The later students stay up at night, the harder they will find it to focus in class.
The more advanced medical technology is, the longer people can live.

points.title: so that 以便  (表目的的副詞子句)
examples: I keep a diary so that I can relive memorable moments in the future.
He set the alarm clock so that he wouldn’t oversleep.

items.sentence: It *has probably happened* to you before.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Prepositional phrase + Adverb

items.sentence: The glass doors of the convenience store *slide* open invitingly; you *hear* the familiar "Welcome!" and *enter* just to pick up one item.
items.pattern: S + Vl + C + Adverb + S + Vt / Vi (Compound predicate) + O + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: A few minutes later, you *walk out* with a whole bag full of drinks, snacks, and other goodies you never even thought of buying!
items.pattern: Adverbial phrase + S + Vi (Phrasal verb) + Prepositional phrase + Relative clause

items.sentence: There *is* no need to be embarrassed if you've experienced this sudden urge to shop.
items.pattern: There + Vi + S + Infinitival phrase + Adverbial clause (if...)

items.sentence: Convenience stores *use* certain strategies to make you feel this way.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: One of these strategies *is* to follow the "eye level is buy level" rule.
items.pattern: S + Vi + Infinitival C

items.sentence: The more visible the products are, the easier it *is* for shoppers to notice and purchase them.
items.pattern: Correlative comparative clause + It + Vl + C + Infinitival phrase

items.sentence: Therefore, smart shop owners usually *place* their most profitable and popular items at the average shopper's eye level to make sure that those items are most likely to be seen.
items.pattern: S + Vt + O + Prepositional phrase + Infinitival phrase + Noun clause (that...)

items.sentence: Similarly, products that are aimed at children, such as toys, *are placed* on lower shelves so that younger shoppers will surely see them.
items.pattern: S + Relative clause (that...) + Appositive phrase + Passive verb phrase + Adverbial clause (so that...)

items.sentence: Another eye-catching convenience store strategy *is* to promote impulse purchases of small, cheap items like candy bars.
items.pattern: S + Vl + Infinitival C

items.sentence: These *are displayed* near cash registers and *are* thus easily noticed and within quick reach.
items.pattern: S + Passive / Linking verb phrases (Compound predicate) + C

items.sentence: Special offers, like "buy one, get one free," *make* such little "extras" even more attractive.
items.pattern: S + Parenthetical example + Vt + O + C

items.sentence: Since customers are lining up at cash registers to pay for their things anyway, these items *can easily be grabbed and added* to their shopping baskets on impulse.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Since...) + S + Passive compound verb phrase + Prepositional phrases

items.sentence: A third strategy *is* to make customers spend more time in stores so that they will spend more money, too.
items.pattern: S + Vl + Infinitival C + Adverbial clause (so that...)

items.sentence: Studies *have shown* that the longer people stay inside, the more products they buy.
items.pattern: S + Vt + Noun clause (that...) with Correlative comparative clauses

items.sentence: Shops *take advantage of* this by setting up bar-style seating or dining areas.
items.pattern: S + Vt (Phrasal verb) + O + Gerund phrase

items.sentence: Here, people *can read* the paper, *hold* a meeting, or just *hang out*.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vt / Vi (Compound predicate) + O

items.sentence: Although these customers might start off with just a beverage, they often *grow* hungry over time.
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (Although...) + S + Vl + C + Adverbial phrase

items.sentence: Eventually, they *end up* purchasing more things like microwave dinners and fruit packs.
items.pattern: Adverb + S + Vi (Phrasal verb) + Gerund phrase

items.sentence: To avoid falling into any of the traps above, *try* to be more aware of the clever strategies convenience stores use to get deeper into your pocket.
items.pattern: Infinitival phrase + Imperative verb + Infinitival phrase + Relative clause

items.sentence: If you can always remember the tricks that shop owners use, you *won't have to worry* about spending too much!
items.pattern: Adverbial clause (If...) with Relative clause + S + Modal verb phrase + Prepositional phrase

text_genre.raw_text: The text of “Convenience Stores” is an informative piece presenting information regarding the three marketing strategies employed by convenience stores to delve deeper into a customer’s pocket. The three strategies are presented and explained one by one: eye level is buy level, promoting impulse purchases, and encouraging customers to spend more time in stores. To avoid falling into any of the traps mentioned above, customers need to be aware of these tricks and stay alert while shopping.
